papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: AI Agent-Driven Framework for Automated Product Knowledge Graph Construction in E-Commerce
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of e-commerce platforms generates vast amounts of unstructured product data, creating significant challenges for information retrieval, recommendation systems, and data analytics. Knowledge Graphs (KGs) offer a structured, interpretable format to organize such data, yet constructing product-specific KGs remains a complex and manual process. This paper introduces a fully automated, AI agent-driven framework for constructing product knowledge graphs directly from unstructured product descriptions. Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), our method operates in three stages using dedicated agents: ontology creation and expansion, ontology refinement, and knowledge graph population. This agent-based approach ensures semantic coherence, scalability, and high-quality output without relying on predefined schemas or handcrafted extraction rules. We evaluate the system on a real-world dataset of air conditioner product descriptions, demonstrating strong performance in both ontology generation and KG population. The framework achieves over 97\% property coverage and minimal redundancy, validating its effectiveness and practical applicability. Our work highlights the potential of LLMs to automate structured knowledge extraction in retail, providing a scalable path toward intelligent product data integration and utilization.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

literature_themes.theme: Integration of Chaos Theory in Deep Learning
literature_themes.summary: This cluster explores the application of homogeneous chaos theory to enhance the understanding and performance of Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANNs). Additionally, the complexity of integrating chaos theory with existing deep learning frameworks poses challenges.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights a novel approach to understanding DANNs, which can help identify gaps in current deep learning methodologies and inspire future research on alternative architectures and learning mechanisms.

summary: The retrieved literature highlights the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction across various domains, particularly in biomedical literature and e-commerce. Key themes include advancements in GNN methodologies, the application of machine learning in materials science, and the theoretical exploration of chaos theory in deep learning. Limitations such as the lack of empirical validation, domain-specific applicability, and challenges in interpretability underscore significant research gaps, indicating a need for comprehensive studies that enhance accuracy and generalizability in knowledge discovery frameworks.
scholarly_positioning: While existing literature has made strides in integrating Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction, significant limitations persist, particularly in empirical validation and domain generalizability. Prior studies, such as those focusing on biomedical literature, often lack comprehensive evaluations across diverse datasets, leaving a gap in understanding how these methodologies can be effectively adapted for broader scientific literature. Furthermore, the theoretical explorations of GNNs, including hyperbolic geometry, remain untested in practical applications, highlighting a critical need for empirical studies that validate these frameworks. This proposed research aims to address these unresolved tensions by developing a robust GNN-based framework specifically tailored for large-scale knowledge discovery in scientific literature, thereby contributing to the advancement of knowledge extraction methodologies and enhancing their applicability across various domains.
research_scope: This study will empirically validate a Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework specifically designed for knowledge extraction from large-scale scientific literature, focusing on biomedical and materials science domains. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the GNN framework will be compared against existing knowledge extraction methods, such as traditional machine learning and rule-based approaches. Primary outcomes will include accuracy and interpretability of extracted knowledge, measured through metrics like F1-score and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC). Secondary outcomes will assess the generalizability of the GNN framework across diverse datasets, including various scientific publications. Controlled experiments will utilize a range of literature datasets to ensure robust comparisons and ablation studies will be conducted to determine the impact of different GNN architectures on performance.
concept_definition: 1. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs): A type of neural network designed to process data structured as graphs, enabling the extraction of relational information from nodes and edges. 2. Knowledge Extraction: The process of identifying and retrieving relevant information from unstructured data sources, such as scientific literature, using automated methods. 3. Empirical Validation: The systematic testing and evaluation of a GNN framework against established methods to assess its performance and reliability. 4. Baseline Comparisons: Evaluating the GNN framework against existing knowledge extraction techniques to establish performance benchmarks. 5. Ablation Studies: Experimental analyses that isolate and evaluate the impact of specific components or architectures within the GNN framework on overall performance. 6. Controlled Experiments: Structured studies using predefined datasets to ensure consistent conditions for comparing the GNN framework's effectiveness. 7. Evaluation Metrics: Quantitative measures such as F1-score and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) used to assess the accuracy and interpretability of extracted knowledge. 8. Generalizability: The ability of the GNN framework to perform effectively across various datasets and scientific domains beyond the training data. 9. Interpretability: The degree to which the outputs of the GNN framework can be understood and explained, often assessed through methods like attention visualization or explanation generation. 10. User Trust: The confidence users have in the GNN framework's outputs, influenced by factors such as perceived transparency and trust calibration. 11. Safety Outcomes: Metrics that evaluate the risk of harmful outputs from the GNN framework, including unsafe response rates and harmful compliance. 12. Internal Representations: The hidden states or activations within the GNN that capture learned features from the input data, which can be analyzed for interpretability. 13. Explanation Generation: The process of creating understandable justifications for the GNN's outputs, aimed at researchers or end-users to enhance trust and usability.
technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible but requires several resources. It necessitates access to open-source GNN models for empirical validation and hidden-state extraction to analyze internal representations. Additionally, labeled datasets are essential for training and evaluation, and controlled experiments will require diverse scientific literature datasets. The study may also benefit from GPU resources for efficient model training. If user trust is a focus, a human-subject design will be needed, along with trust calibration measures. A feasible adjustment would be to ensure access to open-source models and datasets, and to incorporate user trust evaluation through surveys or interviews.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction in biomedical literature; however, they treat the empirical validation of these methodologies across diverse scientific domains as unresolved, leaving unclear whether the performance and interpretability of GNNs can be generalized beyond specific contexts. This matters theoretically because it limits the understanding of GNN capabilities in broader applications, and practically because it hinders the development of robust knowledge extraction frameworks. Therefore, this study investigates the empirical validation of a GNN framework for large-scale knowledge discovery in scientific literature, focusing on its adaptability and effectiveness across various datasets.
question: How does the performance and interpretability of a Graph Neural Network framework for knowledge extraction from large-scale scientific literature compare to traditional machine learning methods in terms of accuracy and generalizability across diverse datasets?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the impact of a Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework (independent variable) on knowledge extraction performance (dependent variable) across diverse scientific literature datasets. The mediator in this causal chain is the internal representations generated by the GNN, which capture relational information and enhance interpretability. The theoretical framework is grounded in machine learning principles, particularly focusing on the adaptability of GNNs in knowledge discovery. System-level outcomes, such as accuracy and generalizability, are influenced by the quality of representation features, while user-level outcomes, including satisfaction and reliance, are mediated by perceived transparency of the GNN outputs. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of GNN adaptations across domains and the relationship between representation quality and user perceptions of trust and satisfaction.
hypothesis: The performance of a Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework (independent variable) for knowledge extraction will significantly outperform traditional machine learning methods (baseline) in terms of accuracy (primary dependent variable), with the internal representations generated by the GNN mediating this effect, leading to enhanced interpretability and generalizability across diverse scientific literature datasets.

The methodology involves controlled experiments using diverse labeled datasets to ensure robust comparisons against traditional machine learning methods, such as support vector machines and rule-based approaches. Key operationalized variables include knowledge extraction performance measured by F1-score and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), while internal representations will be assessed through probing accuracy and activation separability. proposal: This research proposal aims to empirically validate a novel Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework specifically designed for large-scale knowledge extraction from scientific literature, focusing on the biomedical and materials science domains. Unlike prior studies that primarily address knowledge extraction in narrow contexts, this research will systematically evaluate the GNN framework's performance across diverse datasets, addressing the critical gap in empirical validation and generalizability highlighted in the literature. The proposed framework integrates advanced GNN architectures with mechanisms for enhanced interpretability, hypothesizing that the internal representations generated by the GNN will mediate improvements in knowledge extraction performance, thereby increasing user trust and satisfaction. The research question investigates how the GNN framework's accuracy and interpretability compare to traditional machine learning methods, such as support vector machines and rule-based approaches, which often lack the relational understanding necessary for effective knowledge extraction. Methodologically, the study will utilize controlled experiments with clearly defined baselines, including traditional methods and ablation studies to isolate the impact of specific GNN components. Key operationalized constructs will include knowledge extraction performance measured by F1-score and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), internal representations assessed through probing accuracy, and user trust evaluated via surveys. This approach ensures reproducibility and addresses confounding variables by standardizing dataset quality and explicitly incorporating user trust evaluations. Expected contributions include theoretical insights into the relationship between GNN representations and knowledge extraction performance, technical advancements in GNN architecture tailored for scientific literature, and empirical evidence supporting the efficacy of GNNs over traditional methods. By addressing unresolved limitations in existing methodologies, this study aims to significantly enhance the understanding and application of GNNs in knowledge extraction, ultimately contributing to more robust frameworks applicable across various scientific domains.

The study is technically feasible, requiring access to open-source GNN models and diverse labeled datasets for robust evaluation. Scholarly positioning highlights the need for comprehensive empirical studies to address gaps in the generalizability and interpretability of GNN applications across various scientific domains. proposal_critique.revision_plan: Revise the gap stage to clarify the uniqueness and significance of the identified gap. Strengthen the scholarly positioning by critically comparing existing methodologies and highlighting unresolved tensions. Enhance the theoretical mechanism by providing a more detailed explanation of why GNN adaptations should improve performance, and ensure all constructs are operationally defined with clear measurement instruments.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong and clear research framing with minor conceptual weaknesses
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal clearly defines the research problem of knowledge extraction using GNNs, but lacks specificity in operational definitions of key concepts like 'user trust' and 'interpretability'. Major weaknesses: Key concepts are not fully operationalized, leading to potential ambiguity in understanding their implications. Next band requirements: To move into the next band, the proposal should provide explicit operational definitions for all key constructs and clarify the boundaries of the research problem.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: mostly coherent with minor reasoning gaps
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal presents a logical flow from problem to hypothesis, but some assumptions regarding the effectiveness of GNNs are not sufficiently justified. Major weaknesses: The causal claims regarding internal representations mediating performance improvements need stronger empirical support. Next band requirements: Strengthening the justification for causal claims and ensuring all assumptions are backed by literature would enhance coherence.

rubric_scores.level: 15-17: clear novelty with meaningful research differentiation
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal introduces a novel GNN framework tailored for knowledge extraction, distinguishing it from existing methods, but lacks a comprehensive exploration of how it advances theoretical understanding. Major weaknesses: While the technical contribution is clear, the theoretical implications could be articulated more explicitly. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal should elaborate on the theoretical contributions and how they advance the field.

The methodology is generally sound, with clear experimental designs, but lacks detailed descriptions of baseline comparisons and controls. Major weaknesses: Insufficient detail on how confounding variables will be controlled and the specific metrics to be used for evaluation. Next band requirements: Providing a more detailed methodology, including specific baseline methods and controls, would improve the score.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong literature grounding with good comparative analysis
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal engages with relevant literature but primarily summarizes existing work without deeply analyzing gaps or tensions. Major weaknesses: Lacks a critical synthesis of how the proposed research addresses unresolved issues in the literature. Next band requirements: A deeper critical analysis of existing literature and a clearer identification of research gaps would elevate the score.

rubric_scores.level: 7-8: approaching PhD-level with some shallow areas
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates some theoretical depth but lacks comprehensive discussions of limitations and failure modes. Major weaknesses: Limited discussion on potential failure cases and trade-offs in methodology. Next band requirements: Incorporating a more thorough discussion of limitations and failure analysis would strengthen the proposal.

The writing is generally clear and well-structured, but some terminology could be more precise. Major weaknesses: Minor inconsistencies in terminology and some areas of redundancy. Next band requirements: Improving precision in terminology and eliminating redundancies would enhance clarity.

evaluation.comments: Total score: 78.0/100. Academic level: Master-level. Major strengths: Clear identification of a relevant research problem.; Innovative integration of GNNs for knowledge extraction.; Strong methodological framework with empirical validation. Major weaknesses: Insufficient operationalization of key concepts.; Lack of detailed baseline comparisons and controls.; Limited theoretical framing and critical literature engagement. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Provide explicit operational definitions for all key constructs.; Strengthen causal claims with empirical support.; Enhance theoretical contributions and critical literature analysis. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential but lacks the depth and rigor expected of true PhD-level research, requiring significant improvements to meet high academic standards.
